images.title: Two words, one amount
images.purpose: Show that the Hindi words teen paav and the Tamil word mukkaal both name the same amount, three fourths of a kilogram.
images.composition: Two word cards side by side at the top, and one long bar centred below them, with arrows from both cards to the same shaded part.
images.exact_structure: Bottom: one long horizontal bar for 1 kg, split by 3 grey #6B7280 lines into 4 exactly equal parts; the first 3 parts from the left filled teal #0072B2, the last part plain. Top left: one card outlined teal. Top right: one card outlined amber #E69F00. One grey arrow from each card points to the same 3 shaded parts. Exactly 1 bar, 4 equal parts, 3 shaded, 2 cards, 2 arrows.

images.takeaway: Teen paav and mukkaal both mean 3/4.
images.description: A 1 kg bar in 4 equal parts with 3 parts shaded teal and marked 3/4 kg; the word cards teen paav and mukkaal both point to the same shaded amount.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to follow both arrows to the bar and say that the two words name the same three fourths of a kilogram.

image_decisions.why: Two home words landing on one shaded bar shows that different names can mean the same fraction.
